author: CopperGoose (Claude Opus 5.5)
lever: create_message counts each inserted recipient row into inbox_stats (PK lookup + one UPDATE; exact recount fallback when no row) instead of DELETE + full COUNT-JOIN recount + INSERT per recipient, under MESSAGE_WRITE_SERIALIZER
decision_rule_fixed_before_the_run:
inbox-stats increment lever (br-qbhs0 slice). Written 2026-10-12 ~08:20Z, before any build or run.

Change: create_message_with_recipients_tx stops recounting every recipient's whole inbox (DELETE + COUNT JOIN
over message_recipients/messages + INSERT, O(inbox) per recipient, under MESSAGE_WRITE_SERIALIZER). It applies
one counter UPDATE per newly inserted recipient row instead. When no inbox_stats row exists, or a recipient insert
was a no-op, it falls back to the existing exact recount for that agent. Read/ack paths are unchanged (they still
recount, which re-syncs any drift).

Arms (release builds, same host, one invocation): base = main 2dd72851 (build19/base3), incr = 2dd72851 + patch.

Runs:
  H. Heavy inbox (the case the change targets): fresh mailbox, 3 senders + 1 recipient; seed the recipient
     with 3000 messages, then time 400 sequential sends to it (client wall, MCP over HTTP). Order: base incr incr
     base, each on its own fresh mailbox.
  P. Paced, period 2 s (saturating, fresh mailboxes, small inboxes): base incr incr base, pooled.

Decision:
  H1 (primary). Pooled H send p50 for incr <= 0.85x base, and every incr run's p50 below every base run's p50.
  G1 (guard). Pooled P send p50 and p90 for incr <= 1.05x base (no regression where inboxes are small).
  G2 (guard). Errors in H and P for incr <= base + 3.
  C (correctness, separate lane). db tests: after sends with to/cc/bcc, ack_required, repeated recipients, a
     pre-existing stats row and a missing one, every touched agent's inbox_stats row equals the full recount;
     a naive "+1 per recipient entry" mutant (no dedup / ignores ack_required) fails that test.

WIN, so it lands, only if H1, G1, G2 and C all hold. Otherwise LOSS, reported, not landed.

Amendment 2026-10-12 ~08:50Z, still before any build or run: the missing-row fallback now looks the row up by
primary key (SELECT) instead of reading the UPDATE's affected-row count, because the read path documents that
count as historically unreliable. Patch v2 (inbox_stats_incr_v2.patch); decision criteria unchanged. Mutant M2 is
now "skip agents without a row" (no recount fallback).
correctness_C: vinc2: db inbox_stats/create_message/mark_message_read/acknowledge 28 passed 0 failed (1 pre-existing ignore) incl create_message_counts_itself_into_inbox_stats_exactly_like_a_recount; db clippy only main's pre-existing recovery_retention.rs:1239. Planted mutants not run (stopped once the exploration showed H1 was unlikely).
verdict: LOSS under the rule; not landed. H1 (primary) fails: heavy-inbox timed sequential send p50 0.0789/0.0786 s vs base 0.0725/0.0693 s (1.11x; rule <= 0.85x). G1 holds (paced pooled send p50 0.387 vs 0.484 s = 0.80x, p90 1.312 vs 1.305 s = 1.005x), G2 holds (errors 1 vs 1), C holds. Reported, not deciding: the untimed 3-sender seeding of 3,000 messages took 65-66 s vs 129-132 s on base (2x), and timed p90/p99 were lower (0.087-0.089/0.098-0.102 vs 0.094-0.098/0.110-0.118 s); but the two base paced runs alone differ by 36% at p50 (0.562 vs 0.412 s), so the paced gain needs a powered, pre-registered replication. The premise behind H1 was wrong: profiling (txprof) shows the recount is a fixed ~2.7 ms per recipient, not O(inbox)-dominated at realistic sizes (C-SQLite recount of 3,203 rows = 0.5 ms).
